open7.question: 0x28e6f4 strlen + 0x28e708 malloc(494) + 0x28e714 strcpy -> [r4,#0x10]: is this a deep copy of spEvent.stringValue or another field, and can it double free against spEvent_dispose?
open7.answer: It IS spEvent.stringValue, at +0x10, and there is NO double-free risk.
evidence: spEvent_create's record is _calloc(1,20) = five words; it writes only +0x00 (data) and +0x04 (time) (0x285b68/0x285b6c).
The frame reader fills exactly the remaining three: +0x08 int (0x28e6cc), +0x0c float (0x28e6e0), +0x10 the copy (0x28e710). No other field exists.
spEvent_dispose destroys +0x10 and then self (0x285b80 ldr r0,[r0,#0x10] ; 0x285b84 bl _free ; 0x285b90 b _free) — +0x10 is the only owned pointer besides the object.

_spEventTimeline_dispose 0x2813c0 walks frameCount (+0x08), calls spEvent_dispose on each events[i] (0x2813e8 bl 0x285b78), then frees events (+0x10) and times (+0x0c): one dispose, one free of the line-494 block.

The source is Json_getString(frame,"string", eventData+0x0c): either the JSON string_value or EventData's OWN line-1034 block. The copy is unconditional when that result is non-NULL, so event+0x10 never aliases eventData+0x0c; spEventData_dispose frees +0x0c and spEvent_dispose frees +0x10, two distinct allocations.
B18 then disposes the whole root Json tree before returning the data, which is why the copy is mandatory: an alias into the tree or into EventData would dangle once the tree is gone.
